messages:
infra-bot: ALERT: Node tremor-wn-12 transitioned to NotReady (kubelet restart) at 2026-03-15T09:01:41Z. Affected namespace: inference-prod, ~42 pods (inference-pool-usw). Pager routed to dev-oncall. severity=P1 :rotating_light:

dev-oncall: ACK — I'm on it. Can someone grab GPU/driver logs? Any recent infra pushes in us-west-2?

samira: grabbing logs now. quick dump: `journalctl -u kubelet --since "5m" | tail -n 200` shows repeated kubelet restarts. Node dmesg shows `NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus` and multiple kernel oops around 09:00. Containers for model-serving pods exited with code 137 + OOMKill entries.

alex.g: Confirmed from metrics: inference-pool-usw pod restart count spiked at 09:00. 95p latency for model-large-gen jumped from 120ms -> 3.4s. Fallback model-medium started throwing OOMs as well when concurrency hit 12.

sarah: Customer impact: two customers (cust-omega, cust-kite) posted degraded responses; error-rate 502s + timeout has +3.2% across hosted endpoints. No complete service outage yet.

ops-lead: Runbook: isolate node, cordon & drain, scale fallback capacity, and steer traffic. Who can cordon/drain tremor-wn-12? Also notify kernel/driver team — this looks driver-ish.

samira: I'm running cordon/drain now. steps: ```
kubectl cordon tremor-wn-12
kubectl drain tremor-wn-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force --grace-period=30
```

infra-bot: AUTOPILOT: Starting gradual reroute: shifting 20% of inference-pool-usw traffic to inference-fallback-us-east-1. Policy: latency-preference -> cost-tier fallthrough. Logs: `router: reroute(20%) -> us-east-1`

alex.g: While draining, bumping fallback replicas and adding OOM headroom: ```
kubectl scale deploy/inference-fallback --replicas=8 -n inference-prod
kubectl patch deploy/inference-fallback -n inference-prod --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/limits/memory","value":"6Gi"}]'
``` Will watch memory OOMs.

samira: drain completed — node cordoned, pods evicted. A few stateful inference workers restarted into other nodes. Not seeing kernel panic now but GPUs on that host show ECC errors in dmesg. Collecting `nvidia-smi -q` and driver logs for kernel-team.

dev-oncall: Good. Current mitigation summary: tremor-wn-12 cordoned/drained, fallback scaled to 8, router shifted 20% to us-east-1. Latency partially stabilized but still ~1.1s 95p for model-large-gen. Customer impact: degraded latency for cust-omega and cust-kite; no total outage.

sarah: I've opened a customer incident channel to update the two affected customers — will send a short status update: we identified host-level GPU/driver instability, mitigation in progress, ETA for full mitigation TBD.

ops-lead: Handoff in 15m. @alex.g will take next oncall. dev-oncall please include runbook link and the following follow-ups: 1) ticket to kernel/driver team with logs (attach `nvidia-smi` + dmesg) 2) investigate if recent infra kernel/driver rollout overlapped with this host 3) plan a targeted rehypothecation of suspicious host pool.

alex.g: Acknowledged — I'll take the next rotation. Leaving watch on router policies for the next hour. If OOMs persist after scaled headroom, we'll temporarily lower concurrency for model-large-gen to avoid cascading OOMs (quick patch below).```yaml
# temp concurrency controller
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  model-large-gen.maxConcurrency: "8"
```

infra-bot: NOTE: autoscaler observed 2 additional nodes in the us-west-2 inference pool flapping (kubelet restarts) in the last 4m. Recommended: pause automated rolling upgrades for pool for 1h. Command: `infra control update-pool --name=inference-usw --suspend-rolling=true`

samira: collecting artifacts: attached logs saved to s3://redwood-infra/incident-5091010101/ (driver-logs.tar.gz, kubelet-journal.txt, nvidia-smi-output.txt). Pushed PagerDuty incident: https://pd.incident/RED-5091010101

dev-oncall: Handoff: dev-oncall -> alex.g at 09:15Z. Current state: mitigations applied, cordoned host isolated, fallback scaled, router reroute live. Next actions for oncall: monitor OOM/restart counts, watch customer updates, coordinate kernel/driver team remediation, and prepare rollback of routing when stable.

ops-lead: After action items: create post-incident ticket, include timeline + suggestion to quarantine similar hosts and run driver health checks across region. :thumbsup:

alex.g: Taking over. I'll stay pinned for 45m and then hand to night-oncall. If anything regresses, page me immediately.

dev-oncall: closing active pager for this thread — monitoring continues. :white_check_mark:
